dispositions.topic_text: Whether owner form field names must be unique and how duplicate rows are rejected and tested
dispositions.what: OWNER_FORM_FIELDS is keyed by name in State 6 (70_data_provider_closure.json, key [name]): every name is unique across the whole table. Options: unique across the table; unique within request and within values; duplicates resolved by context. Consequences: one key keeps the page and the reader on one row per name; scoped or context-resolved names would need the carrier on the wire. Every option must keep: a submitted name picks at most one row.
options: Require every row name to be globally unique and refuse a release containing duplicates
Require uniqueness separately within request and values
Allow duplicate names and define deterministic row-selection or multi-destination behavior
consequences: Global uniqueness makes ambiguous releases invalid and requires a rejection test.
Scoped uniqueness permits the same submitted name in different carriers and needs a carrier-selection rule.
Allowed duplicates require deterministic parsing and destination semantics.
